dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A local predicate `LocalDef001 μ X K` on a measure space (Ω, MeasurableSpace Ω) with μ : Measure Ω, a real-valued function X : Ω → ℝ, and a real parameter K. It unfolds to the conjunction of five clauses: (1) X is measurable; (2) 0 < K; (3) X is μ-integrable; (4) ∫ X dμ = 0 (X is centered); (5) for every real λ with |λ| ≤ K⁻¹, the function ω ↦ exp(λ · X ω) is μ-integrable and ∫ exp(λ X) dμ ≤ exp(K² λ²). In words: X is a centered, integrable, measurable random variable whose moment generating function exists and is bounded by exp(K²λ²) on the symmetric interval |λ| ≤ 1/K — the standard 'sub-exponential with parameter K' / Bernstein-type MGF condition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Assumed for every index i via `∀ i, LocalDef001 μ (X i) (K i)`. It is the sole structural hypothesis on the summands: it supplies measurability of each X i (hence measurability of the linear combination and of the tail event), positivity of each K i, centering (E[X i] = 0), and the local MGF bound with parameter K i that makes the two-regime Bernstein bound in the conclusion meaningful. Note the MGF bound uses exp(K²λ²) with no factor 1/2, and the admissible λ-range is |λ| ≤ 1/K.

binders: c : ℝ — a real constant, bound by the outermost existential quantifier, i.e. chosen before (and hence uniformly in) the index type ι, the sample space Ω, the measure μ, the random variables X, the parameters K, the coefficients a, and the threshold t. (The two universe parameters u_1 for ι and u_2 for Ω are free at declaration level, so strictly speaking c is fixed only for each pair of universe levels.)
ι : Type u_1 — implicit index type of the family.
Ω : Type u_2 — implicit sample space.
[MeasurableSpace Ω] — instance: Ω carries a σ-algebra.
μ : Measure Ω — implicit measure on Ω.
X : ι → Ω → ℝ — implicit family of real-valued functions on Ω (random variables), indexed by ι.
K : ι → ℝ — implicit family of real parameters, one per index.
a : ι → ℝ — implicit family of real coefficients, one per index.
hne : (Finset.univ : Finset ι).Nonempty — explicit hypothesis that ι is inhabited; it is also used as data, being fed to Finset.sup' in the conclusion.
t : ℝ — implicit threshold, bound after the three main hypotheses, so the bound holds for all t satisfying 0 ≤ t with the same c.
hypotheses: For every index i ∈ ι: LocalDef001 μ (X i) (K i), i.e. (a) X i is Borel measurable; (b) K i > 0; (c) X i is μ-integrable; (d) ∫ X i dμ = 0 (X i is centered); (e) for every real λ with |λ| ≤ (K i)⁻¹, the function ω ↦ exp(λ · X i ω) is μ-integrable and ∫ exp(λ · X i) dμ ≤ exp((K i)² λ²).

The family (X i)_{i ∈ ι} is mutually independent with respect to μ (ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun, with the Borel σ-algebra on ℝ on each coordinate). This is joint independence of the whole family, strictly stronger than pairwise independence.
0 < ∑_{i ∈ ι} (a i · K i)². (Since each K i > 0, this is equivalent to a i ≠ 0 for at least one i; it also guarantees the denominators in the conclusion are nonzero.)
conclusions: μ.real { ω ∈ Ω : | ∑_{i ∈ ι} a i · X i (ω) | ≥ t } ≤ 2 · exp( − c · min( t² / ∑_{i ∈ ι} (a i · K i)² , t / max_{i ∈ ι} ( |a i| · K i ) ) ), where μ.real S denotes (μ S).toReal, the real-valued probability of S, and the maximum is Finset.sup' over the nonempty finset univ (using the hypothesis hne).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X K (the summand condition): X is measurable, K > 0, X is μ-integrable, E_μ[X] = 0, and for all real λ with |λ| ≤ 1/K the variable exp(λX) is μ-integrable with E_μ[exp(λX)] ≤ exp(K²λ²). This is a centered sub-exponential / Bernstein-type moment-generating-function condition with parameter K; note the exponent is K²λ² (no 1/2 factor) and the admissible range of λ is the symmetric interval [−1/K, 1/K].

ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ: mutual independence of the whole family (X i)_{i∈ι} under μ with respect to the Borel σ-algebra on ℝ — for any finite subcollection of indices and any Borel sets, the μ-measure of the intersection of the preimages factors into the product of the individual measures.
MeasureTheory.Measure.real μ S = (μ S).toReal: the real number obtained from the ℝ≥0∞-valued measure; finite here because μ is a probability measure.
Finset.sup' univ hne (fun i => |a i| * K i) = max_{i ∈ ι} (|a i| · K i), the finite maximum over the nonempty index set.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is an absolute positive constant c with the following property. Let ι be a nonempty finite index set and let (Ω, 𝔉, μ) be a probability space. Let X_i : Ω → ℝ (i ∈ ι) be mutually independent random variables such that for each i there is a parameter K_i > 0 with: X_i measurable and integrable, E[X_i] = 0, and E[exp(λ X_i)] ≤ exp(K_i² λ²) (with exp(λX_i) integrable) for every real λ with |λ| ≤ 1/K_i. Let a_i (i ∈ ι) be real coefficients with ∑_i (a_i K_i)² > 0. Then for every t ≥ 0, the two-sided deviation probability of the weighted sum satisfies P( |∑_i a_i X_i| ≥ t ) ≤ 2 exp( − c · min( t² / ∑_i (a_i K_i)² , t / max_i (|a_i| K_i) ) ). In other words, a weighted sum of independent centered random variables satisfying a local sub-exponential MGF bound obeys a Bernstein-type tail inequality with the usual two regimes: sub-Gaussian decay t²/∑(a_iK_i)² for small t and exponential decay t/max_i(|a_i|K_i) for large t, with one universal constant c in the exponent.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The constant c is only asserted to exist and be positive; no numerical value, no upper bound, and no explicit dependence is given. A very small c makes the bound weak but still true, so the statement is strictly weaker than any version with a named constant.

The prefactor 2 makes the bound trivially true whenever 2·exp(−c·min(...)) ≥ 1, in particular at t = 0 (the right-hand side is exactly 2) and for all t below a threshold depending on c. So the statement carries content only in the tail range; a small enough c pushes that range arbitrarily far out. This is the main strength-limiting feature.

The hypothesis 0 < ∑_i (a_i K_i)² excludes the degenerate case a ≡ 0. Given that each K_i > 0 (from LocalDef001), it is exactly the condition that some a_i ≠ 0, which also makes max_i(|a_i|K_i) > 0, so neither denominator in the min is zero and Lean's division-by-zero convention is never triggered. Note, however, that the statement does not need this fact — it is a consequence, not an extra hypothesis.

hne (univ nonempty) rules out ι = ∅. With ι empty the sum hypothesis 0 < 0 would already be false, so hne is not what prevents vacuity; it is present chiefly because Finset.sup' requires a nonemptiness proof as data.
Only mutual independence of the full family is assumed; pairwise independence would not suffice and is not what is written. Conversely nothing weaker (e.g. independence within blocks) is permitted.

No hypothesis constrains the cardinality of ι, so c must be uniform over families of every finite size; likewise nothing constrains the signs of a_i (only |a_i| appears in the max, and a_i appears squared in the sum).
The tail event uses ≥ t rather than > t, so the boundary case is included; the bound is therefore (very slightly) stronger than the strict-inequality version.

Measurability of the tail set is not assumed; it follows from measurability of each X_i inside LocalDef001. μ.real is nevertheless defined on arbitrary sets via the outer measure, so a reader should not read the statement as asserting measurability.

The parameters K_i are supplied as an arbitrary given function, not derived from the X_i. Nothing forces K_i to be sharp (e.g. equal to a sub-exponential norm ‖X_i‖_{ψ₁}); any valid K_i works and larger K_i give weaker conclusions. Correspondingly the statement encodes no relation between K_i and the variance or the ψ₁-norm of X_i.

The two universe levels u_1 and u_2 are free parameters of the declaration, outside the existential. Formally this permits c to differ per universe pair — a formalization artifact with no mathematical significance, but it means 'absolute constant' is universe-relative as stated.

The MGF bound in LocalDef001 uses exp(K²λ²) rather than the more common exp(λ²K²/2); this changes the effective normalization of K and hence the numerical value of the constant c, but not the shape of the statement.
